thought.text: The frontend's server-side `API_URL` must resolve inside the container network. Let me fix it to use the internal backend service name, as the production env template documents (`SCHEMA://BACKEND-CONTAINER-NAME:PORT`).

reasoning_content:
The frontend server-side API_URL needs to be resolvable inside the network. The frontend uses `$env/static/private` API_URL baked at build time. The dev compose passes API_URL default `https://api.localhost/api/v1/`. This is a documented issue—the README note says for the deployment, the production template uses `SCHEMA://BACKEND-CONTAINER-NAME:PORT/API/VERSION`.

But wait — the frontend makes server-side fetches to API_URL. The API_URL must be reachable from the frontend container. `https://api.localhost` isn't resolvable. The recommended value would be `http://backend:8000/api/v1/` or `https://nginx/api/v1/`. But PUBLIC_API_URL (client-side) should remain `https://api.localhost/api/v1/` since the browser resolves that.

However API_URL is baked at build time via build args. So I need to set API_URL=http://backend:8000/api/v1/ (server-side internal) and rebuild the frontend.

Actually, simpler: add a network alias so `api.localhost` resolves to caddy inside the network. But that changes containers. Alternatively set API_URL to internal. Let's check how API_URL is used - it's `$env/static/private` = server side. Let me set API_URL=http://nginx/api/v1/ or http://backend:8000/api/v1/.

Let me look at what the production template suggests: `API_URL=SCHEMA://BACKEND-CONTAINER-NAME:PORT/API/VERSION` -> e.g., `http://backend:8000/api/v1/`. And `PUBLIC_API_URL=SCHEMA://API_DOMAIN/API/VERSION/`.

So the correct config: API_URL=http://backend:8000/api/v1/, PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.localhost/api/v1/. Let me update .env and rebuild frontend.

But wait - if API_URL is http://backend:8000, server-side fetch bypasses caddy and hits backend directly, which is fine.

Let me update .env and rebuild the frontend image.

Also, this is a documented deployment nuance - the guide's primary quick start doesn't set these explicitly; the production .env template shows the container-name URL pattern. So this is a reasonable fix.

Let me do it.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace/deployment && sed -i 's|^API_URL=.*|API_URL=http://backend:8000/api/v1/|' .env && grep -E \"^API_URL|^PUBLIC_API_URL\" .env", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Set internal API_URL for frontend"}
